If you could turn back time to the early days of the internet, would you handle privacy differently? Most of us would — we'd be more careful about which services we used and what information we shared. Since a time machine doesn't exist, we have to face reality. Your personal data is being sold publicly right now.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, and even family relationships are being packaged and sold to marketing companies, insurance firms, and hackers. While Safari and the Mail app have built-in privacy features that block some tracking as you browse, they can't undo years of damage from data collected and scattered across hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry around collecting your data, packaging it up, and reselling it. It's time to take your personal information off the market.

The security risks of the data broker industry

But the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your data is everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber threats. Since this industry is essentially unregulated, your most private information — including past employment history, places you've lived, previous loan records, and more — can be easily purchased. This poses a significant security concern.

Modern scammers use broker-held data to craft highly personalized (and hard-to-spot) phishing attacks. When fraudsters already know your job title, where you've lived, and even the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your natural defenses. If a scammer knows you intimately, the moment you let your guard down even slightly, their chances of success are extremely high.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function like an open, searchable database — a tool for stalkers and harassers. By mapping the relationships between your friends, family, and neighbors, brokers provide a blueprint for locating people trying to stay under the radar and out of the spotlight.

The solution: use Incogni to automatically remove your data

The scale of this ecosystem is staggering, and frankly, demoralizing. Trying to manually request removal from hundreds of sites one by one is essentially a full-time job, with a success rate of nearly zero — because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry works and can help you reclaim your right to privacy.

That's why services like Incogni have become an essential tool for your life — both digital and physical. It takes a massive problem (your data being everywhere and sold freely) and turns it into a solved one, offering an all-in-one solution. Instead of spending months tracking down brokers yourself, Incogni handles the tedious, repetitive administrative work of opt-out requests on your behalf. They make sure your data isn't just deleted once, but continuously prevent brokers from trying to re-collect and re-include your information.

The real benefits of data removal for the privacy-conscious

Getting delisted from internet broker databases delivers immediate results for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their leads. Identity thieves typically obtain victim information from broker sites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to find where you live.
